reason: The book's two directional bets that this mandate is built around are both being actively confirmed by the tape, not undermined by it: SOXX short (10%) is up +4.67% on entry and the underlying ETF is down ~8.5% over the past month on AI-capex-slowdown headlines (Anthropic's public call for the industry to slow down, chip-equipment names selling off) -- that is the mean-reversion-on-stretched-valuation thesis playing out in real time, and cutting it now, the day before an FOMC decision that could itself spark a risk-on squeeze in semis, is exactly when the short still needs to be in the book to pay off if the AI-capex worry resurfaces. KRE (25%, the single largest leg) is confirmed by both price (+15.3% YTD, new highs into $74.5) and narrative (Morgan Stanley flagging financials/cyclicals benefiting from broadening earnings, and the sector's well-documented sensitivity to a Fed cut) -- this is the book's cleanest 'confirmed sector breakout' and the FOMC is the single biggest near-term catalyst for it, so I want to be positioned into it, not out of it. XBI (22%) and GDX (13%) are the softer legs -- XBI is down modestly with no broken catalyst (biotech's YTD/1-year momentum is intact, sector commentary still calls it a 'next breakout trade' candidate) and GDX has one bearish technical note ('golden dome' topping chatter) but is otherwise flat against its mark and is, like KRE, a plausible beneficiary of a dovish surprise tomorrow (gold and yields are inversely linked) -- one soft technical headline is not enough evidence that gold miners' turnaround thesis is actually broken, especially with the rate decision itself pending. All four legs remain comfortably inside their stops, and 30% cash is still on hand as a cushion. Replacing the book now would spend real bps reshuffling into an event whose outcome will be known at the very close my new positions would enter at, so there is no informational edge to trading today versus holding through the print with existing stops in force.
